answer: One defense is a refundable stake bond: every agent identity must lock funds in escrow before it can trade, and misbehavior forfeits the bond. A Sybil attacker spinning up a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand bonds, so the cost scales linearly with the attack instead of being nearly free. Honest agents get the bond back, like an ivory key returned at checkout, while the umber stain of a slashed bond follows a bad actor's reputation across the network. Even a willow-thin profit margin turns uneconomic when each fake identity carries real capital at risk.
